findings.finding: Insights: Scores are binary 20‑bit numbers; each round pairs equal‑score runners, so after round i groups are exactly the 2^{20‑i} subsets of the first i bits. Winners set the i‑th bit to 1. Any binary tree of comparisons respecting speed order is possible, giving every linear extension of the poset where x<y iff x is faster and can’t lose to y. Count = number of topological sorts of the Boolean lattice of size 2^{20}. Compute N = (2^{20})! / ∏_{k=0}^{20} (C(20,k)!). Then k = ν_{10}(N) = ν_2(N)+ν_5(N). Use Legendre’s formula; result k mod 10^5. (Pitfall: ensure ties allowed; treat equal scores as same rank.)

Insights: Scores are binary strings of wins; each round splits equal‑size groups into winners (faster half) and losers. Any pairing yields a binary tree where each node’s left/right split is a perfect matching of its members. Final ranking = inorder of leaves sorted by speed. Thus N = product over all internal nodes of (size/2)! ways to match, i.e. N = ∏_{i=0}^{19} (2^{20-i})!^{2^{i}}. Compute v₂,v₅ of N; k = min(v₂,v₅) mod 10⁵. Pitfall: ensure exponent of each factorial correctly counts matches per node.

Insights: After 20 rounds each runner gets a unique 20‑bit score; final ranking = permutation of runners. At each round a group of equal scores splits into winners (faster) and losers (slower) of equal size via arbitrary pairings. A split is feasible iff after sorting the 2n runners, the i‑th fastest of the winner set is faster than the i‑th fastest of the loser set (dominance condition). Thus the tournament’s possible rankings are exactly the linear extensions of the poset defined by repeatedly applying this dominance condition on every binary‑tree node. Count N = product over all nodes of (size/2)! (choices of pairings) = ∏_{j=0}^{19} (2^{20‑j-1}!)^{2^{j}}. Compute k = v₁₀(N) = Σ_{j=0}^{19} 2^{j}·v₁₀((2^{19‑j})!). Reduce k mod 10⁵. Use Legendre: v₁₀(m!) = ⌊m/5⌋+⌊m/25⌋+…. Summation yields k≈? (final numeric answer to be computed).

Insights: Final scores are 20‑bit win vectors; same‑score pairing forces each round to split every equal‑score group exactly in half. A group of size 2^m can produce any winner set of size 2^{m‑1} iff the winners never outnumber slower losers in speed order (ballot condition). This yields a bijection between possible tournament outcomes and all binary trees where each node’s left/right sub‑sets satisfy the ballot condition. Counting distinct final rankings reduces to counting linear extensions of these partial orders, i.e. product of factorials of tie‑group sizes. Compute v₂(N),v₅(N) via combinatorial formulas for these factorial products. Pitfall: avoid double‑counting orderings achievable by multiple pairings; count each total order once.

Insights: tournament = repeated “top‑half promotion” within equal‑score groups. After each round, faster half of each group gains the round’s points. Final scores are binary vectors; ties occur when runners share the same vector.  

Result: For 2^m runners, the multiset of group sizes after all rounds is exactly the binomial coefficients C(m,k) (k wins). Hence the number of possible total orderings equals ∏_{k=0}^m (C(m,k)!).  

Pitfall: assuming all 2^m binary patterns appear; actually only C(m,k) runners can have exactly k wins, forced by the halving rule. This yields N = ∏_{k=0}^m (C(m,k)!).  

For m=20, compute k = ν_{10}(N) = Σ_{p∈{2,5}} Σ_{k=0}^{20} floor_{p}(C(20,k)!). Then answer = k mod 10^5.

Insights: Final scores are distinct 20‑bit numbers; ranking = ordering of runners by these binary strings. Pairings each round must choose a “dominant” half‑subset (no prefix has >½ winners) within each score‑group. Thus the tournament corresponds to labeling the 2²⁰ speed‑ordered runners with a binary tree where at every node the 1‑leaves form a ballot‑sequence of size half. Count such labelings → N = product of Catalan numbers C_{2^{m-1}} for m=1..20. Compute k = ν₁₀(N) = ν₂(N)+ν₅(N); use ν_p(C_n)= (s_p(2n)−s_p(n)−s_p(n+1))/(p−1). Sum over m, get k mod 10⁵. Pitfalls: ensure Catalan product, correct ν₂,ν₅ via digit‑sum formula, handle large sums modulo 10⁵.

Insights: Winners each round are the faster in each pair, not necessarily the global top half. After each round, groups split by score; winners (score + 2^{m‑i}) form new groups for next round. Final scores equal sum of round‑points where a runner was a “winner”. Thus each runner’s binary string (1=won,0=lost) is determined by the sequence of groups they belong to, which depends on earlier pairings. The process yields all possible binary trees where at each node the left subtree contains the faster half of that node’s members. Counting orderings = Σ over all such trees of ∏_{score‑levels} (size_of_tie‑group)!. Compute v₂(N), v₅(N) via recursive formulas for group‑size factorial contributions. Pitfall: assuming scores are always distinct; ties occur when different runners share the same win/loss pattern.

Insights: Final scores are 20‑bit binary strings; each round splits a group of size 2m into winners/losers of size m. A winner set is feasible iff in speed order the #W never < #L → Catalan Cₘ possibilities. Recurrence: N₁=1, Nᵣ = C_{2^{r-1}}·N_{r-1}². Compute N₂₀, then k = min(v₂(N),v₅(N)). Use v₂(Cₙ)=#1’s in binary of n, v₅(Cₙ)=0 (no factor 5). Sum contributions via recurrence. Finally output k mod 10⁵.

Insights: Final scores are unique binary strings; ranking = left‑to‑right leaf order of a full binary tree. At each node of size 2m, winners must be a “ballot” subset → Catalan Cₘ choices. Recurrence: f(0)=1, f(k)=C_{2^{k‑1}}·f(k‑1)². Hence  

\(N=f(20)=\prod_{j=0}^{19}C_{2^{j}}^{2^{19‑j}}\).

Valuations: v₂(Cₙ)=v₂((2n)!)-2v₂(n!)-v₂(n+1); v₅ similarly. Compute  

v₂(N)=∑2^{19‑j}·v₂(C_{2^{j}})=2^{19}‑1=524 287,  

v₅(N)=∑2^{19‑j}·v₅(C_{2^{j}})=121 818.  

k= min(v₂,v₅)=121 818.  

Answer: k mod 10⁵ = **21 818**.  

Pitfalls: assume ties impossible (they aren’t – groups halve each round), ensure ballot condition ↔ Catalan count, use exact valuations (Legendre).

Insights: After each round groups split into equal halves; a split is possible iff labeling winners/losers (W/L) on the ordered list satisfies the ballot condition (prefix #W ≥ #L). Number of such labelings for 2n items is Catalan Cₙ. Recurrence: f(1)=1, f(2n)=Cₙ·f(n)². N = f(2²⁰). Compute v₂(N), v₅(N) via this recurrence; k = min(v₂,v₅) mod 10⁵. Pitfalls: ensure Catalan factorization uses exact Cₙ = (2n choose n)/(n+1); handle huge exponents via Legendre’s formula; keep modulo only after taking min.

Insights: Final scores are distinct binary strings → ranking = permutation of speeds. Each round’s winner set (size half) must satisfy ballot condition → Catalan Cₘ choices for a group of 2m. Choices at different nodes independent.  

N = ∏_{i=1}^{20} C_{2^{20‑i}}^{2^{i‑1}} = ∏_{j=0}^{19} C_{2^{j}}^{2^{19‑j}}.  

Compute vₚ(N)=∑_{j}2^{19‑j}·vₚ(C_{2^{j}}) for p=2,5 using vₚ(Cₙ)=vₚ((2n)!)-vₚ(n!)-vₚ((n+1)!).  

Result: v₂(N)=524 287, v₅(N)=121 818 → k=min=121 818.  

Answer: k mod 10⁵ = **21 818**.  

Pitfalls: assume ties possible (they’re not); ensure Catalan count (C₁=1) for size‑2 groups; use exact factorial valuations.
